title: Design System: Training Unit Command Center

brand.note: Synced with LACE Learning Hub --brand. Interactive signal: links, focus rings, panel ticks, primary buttons.

on-accent.note: The foreground for anything on an accent fill. Synced with LACE Learning Hub.

brand-deep.note: Brand accent darkened for warn-state due dates on hovered rows. Synced with LACE --brand-ink.

display.purpose: The page name, once per page. Geist sans with tight tracking.

headline.purpose: The week range and calendar month on focus pages.

title.purpose: Tool and tile names. Steps down to 15px for document rows, 14.5px for task names.

label.purpose: Panel titles. Uppercase, tracked, always preceded by the brand tick.

eyebrow.purpose: The brand-blue line above every page title. Widest tracking in the system.

meta.purpose: Counts, dates, board names, staleness notes, sync status. Always tabular figures.

themes.note: Light is canonical in tokens.css, synced with LACE Learning Hub globals.css. Dark uses LACE's near-black studio palette. Both selectors must be authored together so the in-page toggle beats the OS preference in both directions.

contrast.binding: WCAG 2.1 AA — 4.5:1 for text, 3:1 for meaningful non-text, per PRODUCT.md
contrast.method: Every foreground/background pair that actually occurs, computed from the token values in both themes. All 52 pass.
contrast.tightest: working dot on paper-2 at 3.09:1 (light) — re-measure if either surface changes.

shadows.name: ambient
shadows.purpose: Panels, header band, results bar, announcement banner. Present at rest and meant to go unnoticed; it marks a container's outer edge, never hierarchy.

shadows.name: ambient-dark
shadows.purpose: The same role in dark mode, with much stronger alphas because a dark ground swallows a 4% shadow.

shadows.name: overlay
shadows.purpose: Defined once, used once: the focus-page dropdown. The only genuinely floating element in the product.

shadows.name: accent-bloom
shadows.purpose: Pin and quick-link rows on hover. A tinted glow in the item's own pigment rather than a neutral shadow.

shadows.name: focus-ring
shadows.purpose: The universal focus-visible treatment. Replaces the default outline and is always paired with the element's hover treatment.

shadows.name: focus-ring-inset
shadows.value: inset 0 0 0 2px color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent, var(--brand)) 45%, transparent)
shadows.purpose: Focus for elements that cannot afford an outer ring — accordion summaries and drill-down sublinks inside a clipped container.

motion.name: state
motion.purpose: The default for tiles, rows, and icon buttons: transform, border-color, background, box-shadow.

motion.name: state-quick
motion.purpose: Smaller objects and controls — task rows, kanban cards, pills, selects, mini buttons.

motion.name: reveal
motion.purpose: The search panel's opacity and 6px translate, and chevron rotation.

motion.name: lift
motion.purpose: Hover for tiles, buttons, and app tiles. 2px for primary tiles, 1px for everything smaller.

motion.name: slide
motion.purpose: Hover for list rows and pin links, which move toward the reader rather than up. Arrows slide 3px independently.

motion.name: reduced
motion.purpose: A blanket reset under prefers-reduced-motion. Because it strips every transition in the product, no state may be communicated by motion alone.

breakpoints.name: xs
breakpoints.purpose: App grid drops to 2 columns; count pills hide; header actions stack.

breakpoints.name: sm
breakpoints.purpose: LMS grid goes single-column; view toggle tightens and spans full width.

breakpoints.name: compact
breakpoints.purpose: Week task rows stack vertically; subfolder columns collapse to one.

breakpoints.name: md
breakpoints.purpose: Task table hides its board column.

breakpoints.name: touch
breakpoints.purpose: The main mobile breakpoint: 48px row minimums, 12px body padding, containers drop from 16px to 12px radius, search panel goes edge-pinned, nav pills go full width.

breakpoints.name: lg
breakpoints.purpose: Kanban goes single-column; calendar cells shrink to 58px.

breakpoints.name: container
breakpoints.purpose: Launcher max width. Focus pages cap at 1100px.

components.name: Tool Tile
components.description: The primary launcher object: a monogram chip, a name, a truncated description, and an arrow. Rests on Kraft and inverts to Fresh Sheet on hover while its border mixes toward the item's own accent.
components.html: GGoogle DriveShared files and folders

components.name: App Tile
components.description: The compact quick-access tile from the Quick Links grid: a centred logo or monogram over a label, three across on desktop and two below 400px.

components.name: Document Row
components.description: The lightest list object: borderless at rest, it gains a Kraft ground and slides 2px toward the reader on hover. Used for standing documents and LMS links.
components.html: Weekly Meeting AgendaStanding agenda for Monday check-ins→

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The only filled brand-blue surface in the product besides the active toggle segment.

components.name: Mini Button

narrative.overview: Warm, precise, unhurried — shared with the LACE Learning Hub. The page is a warm paper field lit by a soft steel-blue wash at the top edge, and everything on it is an object pinned to that field. Per-item accent inheritance drives the wall metaphor; --brand is the fallback for items without their own pigment. Geist sans throughout. Tokens live in tokens.css, synced with LACE globals.css.
keyCharacteristics: Warm cream paper field (#f7f6f2) with a radial brand-blue wash at 8% at the top of every page
Per-item --accent inheritance into four fixed slots: monogram tint, hover border, arrow, focus ring
A three-surface tonal ladder — page → resting object → raised object — that inverts on hover
Hairline 1px borders as the primary structural device; shadow is atmosphere, not hierarchy
Geist sans for all text, including page titles and monogram letters
Uppercase, tracked, 650-weight micro-labels; tabular figures on every count and date
Motion is small and directional: 1–3px lifts and slides over 130–170ms
Full dark counterpart aligned with LACE's near-black studio palette

rules.name: The Four Slots Rule
rules.body: An item's --accent may appear in exactly four places: the monogram chip's tint (12–16% mixed into the card colour), the hover and focus border (30–55% mixed into --line), the arrow or chevron on hover, and the focus ring (35% at 3px). Anywhere else — filled backgrounds, body text, icon strokes at rest, decorative bars — is off the wall.

rules.name: The Status-Isn't-Brand Rule
rules.body: Pine, Ink Blue, Dry Clay, Red Ochre, and Raw Amber encode Monday task state. They never appear as decoration, never as a category colour, and never on the launcher board, which has no task state to express.

rules.name: The Warm-Light, Cool-Dark Rule
rules.body: Light surfaces are warm (hue ~85°) and dark surfaces are cool (hue ~250°), while the accent moves the other way — warmer and lighter in the dark theme. Never port a light-mode neutral into the dark palette by darkening it; the two ladders are separately authored.

rules.name: The On-Accent Rule
rules.body: Never hard-code white on an accent fill. Because the accent lightens in dark mode, white-on-accent inverts from 5.0:1 to 2.7:1 — the label disappears exactly where it used to be strongest. Use --on-accent, which flips to dark ink with the theme.

rules.name: The Every-Colour-Is-A-Token Rule
rules.body: A colour that lives as a hex literal in a rule will never get a dark-mode counterpart, because the dark blocks only redefine tokens. Every one of this system's AA failures came from a literal. If a value is worth writing twice, it is a token.

rules.name: The Sans-Only Rule
rules.body: Geist sans is used for all text, including page titles, week/month frames, and monogram letters. There is no serif voice in this system.

rules.name: The Tracked-Caps Rule
rules.body: Any text at 12px or below that functions as a label is uppercase, tracked 0.04–0.14em, and weight 650–700. Small lowercase text is content, never a label. The inverse also holds: nothing above 14px is ever uppercase.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Every count, date, due value, and item tally carries font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums. Numbers in this system align in columns even when they aren't in a table.

rules.name: The 300px Floor Rule
rules.body: The narrow column never goes below 300px. Below that the layout goes single-column instead of squeezing — a 250px sidebar would break every pin row and task card in it.

rules.name: The 48px Target Rule
rules.body: At 640px and below, every tile, row, accordion summary, and sublink takes min-height: 48px, monograms grow to 36px, and hover transforms are disabled outright under @media (hover: none). Touch gets more room, not the same room.

rules.name: The Line-Not-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Structure is drawn with a 1px --line border. If two elements need visual separation, they get a rule or a tonal step — never a heavier shadow.

rules.name: The Invert-On-Hover Rule
rules.body: An interactive object rests on --paper-2 and becomes --card on hover and focus, while its border mixes toward its own accent. The surface brightening is the affordance; a colour-only hover reads as broken here.

rules.name: The One Overlay Rule
rules.body: --shadow-lg belongs to the single dropdown menu. A new floating panel needs a real justification, not a shadow token.

rules.name: The Tick Rule
rules.body: Every panel title is preceded by a 4×12px brand bar with a 2px radius, and every page eyebrow by the same mark. It is the product's signature — a pin pushed into the wall. A panel title without it is not a panel title.

rules.name: The Radius-Is-Rank Rule
rules.body: 16px containers hold 12px objects hold 10px rows hold 8px controls. A radius larger than its parent's is always wrong.

dos: Do declare an --accent on any new item that represents a distinct tool, project, folder, person, or pin, and let it flow to the four permitted slots only.
Do build hover borders with color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent, var(--brand)) N%, var(--line)) — 30% for document rows, 45% for accordions and app tiles, 55% for primary tiles.

Do pair every :hover with a matching :focus-visible that adds box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent, var(--brand)) 35%, transparent) and removes the default outline. Keyboard users see the pointer treatment plus a ring, never less.
Do rest interactive objects on --paper-2 and raise them to --card, so the tonal ladder stays intact.
Do put font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums on every count, date, and tally.
Do precede every panel title with the 4×12px brand tick.

Do author both dark-mode selectors together — @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) { :root:not([data-theme="light"]) } and :root[data-theme="dark"] — because the toggle must beat the OS in both directions.
Do give rows min-height: 48px below 640px and neutralise hover transforms under @media (hover: none).
Do mark a not-yet-live destination with the soon pattern: 55–62% opacity, a soon tag, and no href at all.

Do reach for a semantic token — --overdue, --danger, --working, --ok, --wait, --on-accent, --brand-deep — instead of a hex literal, and give it a value in all three token blocks (light, prefers-color-scheme: dark, and [data-theme="dark"]).
Do give hover-revealed controls a @media (hover: none) fallback that keeps them visible. An opacity: 0 control still occupies its box and still takes taps.
Do keep a small control's drawn size and grow only its hit area, using a ::after pseudo-element at inset: -3px, so an 18px checkbox is still a 24px target.
Do re-measure both themes when a colour changes. Every AA failure this system has had was dark-mode-only and invisible from a light-mode screenshot.
donts: Don't use a status pigment for anything but Monday task state.
Don't create resting hierarchy with shadow. Two elements at the same tonal step are at the same level, whatever their shadows say.
Don't fill an area with brand beyond the primary button and the active toggle segment. It marks; it does not cover.
Don't set a label lowercase below 12px, and don't set anything uppercase above 14px.
Don't give a child a larger radius than its parent.
Don't treat --faint as a lighter --muted. Choose between them by role, not by appearance.
Don't put a bare outline: none on a :focus rule without a replacement indicator.
Don't let motion be the only carrier of a state change.
Don't add a second dashed border. The dashed --line box means "nothing here yet" and nothing else.
Don't introduce a second accent colour system. Shared tokens live in tokens.css and stay synced with LACE globals.css.
